gloss: pursue, chase, follow after; persecute; strive after
summary: To go after someone to overtake him: an army after a fleeing enemy, Pharaoh after Israel, the avenger of blood after the killer, Saul after David. Of enemies who hound the faithful it is to persecute, and of Yahweh, his curses, or blood it is the judgment that runs a man down; the cursed “flee when no one pursues” (Lev 26:17; Pro 28:1). With an aim for its object it is to strive after: “righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, that you may live and possess the land” (Deu 16:20), peace (Psa 34:15), or empty things (Pro 12:11). Arabic radafa “ride behind, follow” and Akkadian radāpu “pursue, hasten” share the root; the Peshitta's רדַף is “persecute”.

words.gloss: pursue, chase, follow after; persecute; strive after
words.summary: About 140 times, nearly all qal. Its core is going after: it is often followed by אַחֲרֵי “after”, set beside הִשִּׂיג “overtake” (Exo 15:9; Psa 18:38) and against נוּס “flee” (Lev 26:17, 36). Whether the pursuit is to kill, to persecute, or to gain a good depends on what is pursued.

stems.gloss: pursue, chase; persecute; (of judgment) overtake; strive after

senses.definition: To go after a fleeing enemy or person to overtake him: an army in battle, a raiding party, a fugitive. Often with אַחֲרֵי, and with הִשִּׂיג “overtake” for the end of the chase.

evidence.note: “The enemy said, אֶרְדֹּף אַשִּׂיג, I will divide the spoil”: pursue, then overtake.
“Egypt וַיִּרְדְּפוּ after them and overtook them camping by the sea.”
Abram “pursued as far as Dan” after the kings who took Lot.
“He struck them and pursued them to Hobah, north of Damascus.”
“Shall I pursue after this band? Shall I overtake it?” “Pursue, for you shall surely overtake and surely deliver.”
“I pursue my enemies and overtake them, and do not turn back until they are finished.”
“Do not stand still; pursue after your enemies and strike their rear.”
Gideon's three hundred crossed the Jordan “weary, yet pursuing”.
The army of the Chaldeans pursued Zedekiah and overtook him in the plains of Jericho.
The Amorites “chased you as bees do”.
The blessing of obedience: “you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.”
“Five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you ten thousand.”
“One man of you pursues a thousand, for Yahweh your God fights for you.”
Turned round against Israel: “how could one chase a thousand … unless their Rock had sold them?”
The curse: “you shall flee (וְנַסְתֶּם) when no one pursues you”: flight and pursuit as opposites.
“The sound of a driven leaf shall chase them, and they shall flee … and fall when no one pursues.”
“The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are bold as a lion.”
“On the swift we will ride; therefore your pursuers shall be swift.”
“Lest the avenger of blood pursue after the killer while his heart is hot, and overtake him.”
Laban “pursued after him seven days' journey and overtook him” in Gilead.
Joseph to his steward: “pursue after the men, and when you overtake them, say …”.
“Gehazi pursued after Naaman, and Naaman saw one running (רָץ) after him”: going after, not hostile.
Saul hunts David “as one pursues a partridge in the mountains”.

senses.definition: Of enemies who keep after a righteous man to destroy him, often without cause: his “pursuers” (רֹדְפַי) are his persecutors, from whom he asks Yahweh to deliver him.

evidence.note: “Yahweh my God, in you I take refuge; save me from all my pursuers and deliver me.”
“Let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, and trample my life to the ground.”
“The enemy has pursued my soul; he has crushed my life to the ground; he has made me dwell in darkness like the dead of long ago.”
“Princes persecute me without cause (חִנָּם), but my heart fears your words.”
“They persecute me with falsehood; help me.”
“When will you execute judgment on my persecutors?”
“Many are my persecutors and my adversaries, yet I do not turn from your testimonies.”
“My times are in your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and from my pursuers.”
“Deliver me from my pursuers, for they are stronger than I.”
“They persecute him whom you have struck.”
“God has forsaken him; pursue and seize him, for there is none to deliver.”
The wicked man “persecuted the poor and needy … to put him to death”.
David to Saul: “Why does my lord pursue after his servant? What have I done?”
“After whom do you pursue? After a dead dog, after a flea.”
“Avenge me on my persecutors … know that for your sake I bear reproach.”
“Let my persecutors be put to shame, but let me not be put to shame.”
“Yahweh is with me as a dread warrior; therefore my persecutors shall stumble and not prevail.”
“Why do you persecute me as God does, and are not satisfied with my flesh?”
“All her pursuers overtook her between the narrow places.”
“Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the heavens.”
Yahweh will put the curses “on your enemies and on those who hate you, who persecuted you”.

senses.gloss: (of Yahweh, his curse, his judgment) pursue, overtake
senses.definition: Yahweh, his messenger, his storm, the curses of the covenant, or shed blood going after the guilty until they are overtaken.

evidence.note: “All these curses shall come upon you and pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of Yahweh.”
Disease, sword and blight “shall pursue you until you perish”.
“I will pursue after them with the sword, the famine and the plague.”
“You have covered yourself with anger and pursued us; you have killed and not pitied.”
Of Judah's enemies: “pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of Yahweh.”
“Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of Yahweh pursuing them.”
“So pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.”
To Edom: “I will make you blood, and blood shall pursue you; since you did not hate blood, blood shall pursue you.”
Edom “pursued his brother with the sword”: the crime the judgment answers.
“Israel has rejected the good; the enemy shall pursue him.”
“Terrors are turned upon me; they pursue my honour like the wind.”

senses.definition: With a thing for its object: to go after it earnestly to gain it, whether righteousness, peace and the knowledge of Yahweh, or bribes, strong drink and wind.

evidence.note: “צֶדֶק צֶדֶק תִּרְדֹּף, that you may live and possess the land which Yahweh your God gives you.”
“Depart from evil and do good; seek (בַּקֵּשׁ) peace and pursue it”: pursue parallel to seek.
“Listen to me, רֹדְפֵי צֶדֶק, seekers of Yahweh.”
“He who pursues righteousness and covenant faithfulness finds life, righteousness and honour.”
“Let us know, let us pursue to know Yahweh.”
They accuse me (יִשְׂטְנוּנִי) “because I pursue good”.
Psa 34:15 quoted: “let him seek peace and pursue it (διωξάτω)”.
Jerusalem's princes: “everyone loves a bribe and pursues rewards (שַׁלְמֹנִים); they do not judge the orphan.”
“Woe to those who rise early in the morning to pursue strong drink.”
“Ephraim feeds on wind and pursues the east wind all day.”
“Those who pursue wickedness (זִמָּה) draw near; they are far from your law.”
“Will you pursue dry stubble?”: a pursuit not worth the making.

stems.gloss: pursue eagerly, follow after; (of good or evil) pursue a man

senses.definition: To go after a thing or person with persistence: lovers, righteousness, evil, empty things. In Proverbs the participle מְרַדֵּף names a man by what he chases.

evidence.note: “She shall pursue her lovers but not overtake them; she shall seek them but not find them.”
“The way of the wicked is an abomination to Yahweh, but he loves one who pursues righteousness.”
“Righteousness tends to life, but one who pursues evil, to his death.”
“He who works his ground shall be satisfied with bread, but he who pursues empty things lacks heart.”
The same, ending “shall be satisfied with poverty”.
The poor man “pursues with words, but they are gone”: he goes after friends who have left him.

senses.gloss: (goodness, evil, darkness) follow, pursue a man
senses.definition: What a man has earned or been given goes after him and stays with him: goodness and covenant faithfulness, evil, darkness.

evidence.note: “Surely goodness and covenant faithfulness shall pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of Yahweh.”
“Evil pursues sinners, but the righteous are repaid with good.”
“Darkness shall pursue his enemies.”

senses.definition: To be the one chased: Judah under its conquerors, and in Ecclesiastes what has gone by.

evidence.note: “Upon our necks we are pursued; we are weary and have no rest.”
“What will be has already been, and God seeks (יְבַקֵּשׁ) what is pursued”: either the past, driven away, which God calls back, or the one hunted down, whom God seeks out.

senses.definition: Of the nations rebuked by Yahweh: driven off like chaff before the wind.

evidence.note: “He shall rebuke him, and he shall flee far away, וְרֻדַּף like the chaff of the mountains before the wind.”

senses.definition: Once, of Israel against Benjamin: they surrounded him and chased him down.

evidence.note: “They surrounded Benjamin, הִרְדִיפֻהוּ, and trod him down with ease as far as opposite Gibeah.”

evidence.locator: Psa.34.15, וְרָדְפֵהוּ → διώκω; Deu.16.20 → διώκῃ; Isa.51.1; Pro.15.9; Jer.20.11 → διώκω; διώκω renders רָדַף ×28 and more in its other forms

evidence.note: Psa 34:15 quoted: “let him seek peace and pursue (διωξάτω) it.”
Gentiles “who did not pursue righteousness” attained it by faith; Israel “pursuing a law of righteousness” did not: the pursuit of Deu 16:20 and Isa 51:1.
“Pursue peace with all, and holiness, without which no one shall see the Lord.”
“Blessed are those persecuted (δεδιωγμένοι) for righteousness' sake.”

evidence.locator: Gen.14.14 → καταδιώκω; Exo.14.8, 9, 23; Psa.23.6 → καταδιώξεταί; καταδιώκω renders רָדַף ×26 and more in its other forms

evidence.note: “Simon and those with him searched him out (κατεδίωξαν)”: its one New Testament use.

parallels.note: “Overtake”: the end of the pursuit, often in the next clause.
“Seek”: beside pursue of righteousness, peace and lovers.

phrases.gloss: when no one pursues: the flight of the guilty

words.summary: Once, in the taunt over the king of Babylon, in the form of a hophal participle, “pursued”, used as a noun. It stands beside רֹדֶה “ruling” (of רדה), and the line could be read as from that root instead; the form itself is of רדף, and the sense, a pursuit that is not held back, fits the parallel “a striking without turning aside”. One use, so the word rests on little.

senses.definition: A pursuit of the nations by their conqueror that is never held back.

evidence.note: “He who struck the peoples in wrath with a striking that did not turn aside, ruling the nations in anger, מֻרְדָּף בְּלִי חָשָׂךְ”: a persecution none restrained.

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb of the root, for διώκω where it means persecute; where διώκω means pursue an aim (Rom 9:30–31; Heb 12:14; 1Pe 3:11 quoting Psa 34:15) the Peshitta uses רהַט “run after” instead.

senses.definition: To hound the prophets, Jesus, his disciples and his ecclesia, for their faith.

evidence.note: “Blessed are you when they reproach you וְרָדפִין לכֻון and say every evil word against you falsely because of me.”
“So רדַפו the prophets who were before you.”
“Pray for those who lead you away by force וְרָדפִין לכֻון.”
“A servant is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also.”
The Jews “were persecuting Jesus and seeking to kill him” because of the sabbath.
“Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute?”
“Saul, Saul, why רָדֵף אַנתּ me?”
Paul “persecuted the ecclesia of God exceedingly and laid it waste”.
“As then he who was born after the flesh persecuted him who was born after the spirit, so it is now.”
The dragon cast to the earth “persecuted the woman who bore the male child”.

senses.definition: To suffer persecution, the lot of the righteous.

evidence.note: “Blessed are those דֵּאתרדֵפו because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”
“All who will live in the fear of God in Jesus the Messiah מֵתרַדפִין.”

senses.definition: Of clouds driven along by a storm.

evidence.note: “Clouds מֵתרַדפָּן by a tempest” (ἐλαυνόμεναι).

senses.definition: One who persecutes: Paul of himself before his calling, and those whom believers are to bless.

evidence.note: “I was formerly a blasphemer וְרָדֻופ and insolent, but I received mercy.”
“As to zeal, רָדֻופָא of the ecclesia.”
“Bless לרָדֻופַיכֻּון; bless and do not curse.”

senses.definition: Persecution suffered for the word and the ecclesia, named beside affliction (אֻולצָנָא).

evidence.note: “When affliction or רדֻופיָא comes because of the word, at once he stumbles.”
“There was on that day a great persecution against the ecclesia in Jerusalem, and they were all scattered.”
“Who shall separate me from the love of the Messiah? Affliction, or distress, or persecution …?”
A hundredfold now “with persecution, and in the age to come everlasting life”.

senses.definition: The persecutions a believer endures, from which the Lord delivers.

evidence.note: “What persecution I endured, and out of them all my Lord delivered me.”
“Your endurance in all your persecutions and afflictions which you endure.”

cognates.gloss: ride behind another; follow, come after; (ridf) one who follows; (irtadafa al-ʿaduww) take the enemy from behind
cognates.note: The Arabic keeps the going after without the hostility: to come behind and follow. Its eighth form, of an enemy, is to come on him from behind and seize him, the Hebrew's pursue and overtake. Arabic f answers Hebrew p regularly.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1067, art. ردف, رَدِفَهُ (n15259)
evidence.note: “He rode behind him [on the same beast] … he, or it, followed, or came after, him, or it.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1068, art. ردف, اِرْتَدَفَ (8)
evidence.note: “ارتدف العَدُوَّ He took the enemy, or seized him … coming from behind him.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1068, art. ردف, رِدْفٌ (n15264)
evidence.note: “A sequent of a thing.”

cognates.note: Neo-Assyrian: the same verb, with a noun “pursuit” and an adjective “pursued” formed like the Hebrew מֻרְדָּף.

evidence.locator: atae x000012860, radāpu [pursue] V: hasten; pursue; pursuit
SEM000348 rdp [pursue] V, AKK009760 radāpu [pursue] V

cognates.gloss: pursue; (pael) pursue; (passive participle) quick, rapid (of running water)
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the Targums render the Hebrew verb with it, and its passive participle describes water that runs fast, as Akkadian radāpu is also “hasten”.

evidence.locator: s.v. רְדַף (ch.), citing Targ. I Sam. XXIII, 28; Targ. Prov. XIII, 21 (Pa.); Targ. Deut. XVI, 20; Targ. Koh. III, 15; part. pass. רְדִיף quick, rapid, Yoma 77b; B. Bath. 73b

cognates.note: Syriac: “follow” beside “persecute”, the Hebrew's two sides of going after.

evidence.locator: root 1732 RDI; lexemes 2949 RDI (follow; persecute), 2946 RDOIA (persecutor), 2947 RDOI;A and 2948 RD;IOTA (persecution)

doctrine.statement: Israel was commanded, “righteousness, righteousness you shall pursue, that you may live and possess the land which Yahweh your God gives you” (Deu 16:20). “He who pursues righteousness and covenant faithfulness finds life” (Pro 21:21), and Yahweh “loves one who pursues righteousness” (Pro 15:9). Isaiah calls “you who pursue righteousness, you who seek Yahweh” to look to Abraham, the one man Yahweh called and blessed, because “Yahweh will comfort Zion … and make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of Yahweh” (Isa 51:1–3). Hosea's call is “let us pursue to know Yahweh” (Hos 6:3), and the psalm's, “seek peace and pursue it” (Psa 34:15), which Peter quotes to believers (1Pe 3:11); “pursue peace with all, and holiness, without which no one shall see the Lord” (Heb 12:14). Paul says the Gentiles who did not pursue righteousness attained it, the righteousness of faith, while Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain it, “because they sought it not by faith” (Rom 9:30–32). From the verses: the pursuit of righteousness is for life and for the land promised to Abraham, which Yahweh will make like Eden; the righteousness that attains it is by faith, as Abraham's was.

The psalmists and Jeremiah are pursued by enemies “without cause” and “with falsehood”, and cry to Yahweh to deliver them from their pursuers and to judge them (Psa 7:2; 119:84, 86, 161; Jer 15:15; 20:11); Jeremiah bears it “for your sake”. Jesus says, “blessed are those persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven … for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you” (Mat 5:10–12), and “if they persecuted me, they will persecute you also” (Jhn 15:20); “all who will live godly in the Messiah Jesus will be persecuted” (2Ti 3:12). Paul, who had persecuted the ecclesia, heard “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?” (Act 9:4; 1Co 15:9), and sets the pattern back in Abraham's house: “as then he who was born after the flesh persecuted him who was born after the spirit, so it is now” (Gal 4:29; Gen 21:9). The persecuted are to bless and pray for their persecutors (Mat 5:44; Rom 12:14), and Yahweh will put the curses on the enemies “who persecuted you” (Deu 30:7). Their endurance is “that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you suffer”, and the relief comes “when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels” (2Th 1:4–7). From the verses: persecution has been the lot of the faithful from Isaac and the prophets to Jesus and his ecclesia; it is to be borne without revenge, and is answered when Jesus returns to judge and to give the kingdom.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. Root key רדפ; no existing entry used it. BDB keys: t.bc.aa verb, t.bc.ab noun מֻרְדָּף (Isa 14:6). Left unassigned: m.dj.ah and t.az.ab, zero-token cross-references between רדף and רדה for the same Isa 14:6 form. No merged letter in the root, so no sounds. No personal name is formed from the root (TIPNR checked). No Biblical Aramaic word: Daniel and Ezra do not use the root. Psa 38:21 רָדְפִי (ketiv רדופי) is cited in strive-after but is not among the brief's qal tokens; check how the corpus files it. Open questions: (1) Isa 14:6 מֻרְדָּף, a hophal participle, stands beside רֹדֶה “ruling” and may be a scribal variant of a form of רדה (מִרְדַּת “dominion”); kept here by its spelling. (2) Ecc 3:15 נִרְדָּף, “what is pursued”: the past driven away, or the persecuted whom God seeks out; both are given. (3) Job 19:28 נִרְדָּף is qal imperfect first plural (“how we will pursue him”), not niphal. Leads not followed: Ugaritic rdp (DULAT, not vendored), Ge'ez, and Payne Smith for ܪܕܦ “drive” beyond 2Pe 2:17.
